conventions.convention: The geometry is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature (−,+,+,+); the matter domain U is nonempty and open, T is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and n is a smooth future-directed observer field with g(n,n)=−1.
μ=T(n,n), Jᵃ=−Tᵃᵇn_b, Φ=J−μn, hᵃ_b=δᵃ_b+nᵃn_b, and Sᵃᵇ=hᵃ_chᵇ_dTᶜᵈ. In an observer-adapted orthonormal basis Φⁱ=T⁰ⁱ=−T₀ᵢ.
Φ has energy-density component units; the SI energy-flux vector is q=cΦ and the SI momentum-density covector is p=Φ♭/c. Thus q♭=c²p. Measured stress has units Pa.
Acceleration is a=∇ₙn, expansion is θ=∇ₐnᵃ, and Df=nᵃ∇ₐf. The observer-curve parameter is the flow parameter of the unit field; an SI clock reading requires the framework's proper-time conversion.
Flux requires a separately chosen orientation on U and uses its restricted metric volume form. Chains are finite smooth singular chains; no extension of T or J outside U is required.

The Killing current is Jξᵃ=Tᵃᵇξ_b=−XJᵃ and its charge is Qξ(Σ)=−Φ_Jξ(Σ)=Φ_XJ(Σ). The adapted-normal orientation controls the slice sign. Qξ has joule units when ξ's flow parameter has length units; positive constant rescaling of ξ rescales the charge.

The field-law presentations are alternatives; the physical theorem is conditional on adopted assumptions and contains no empirical premise. Positivity and a vanishing side flux are additional conditions, not consequences of divergence-freedom.
The smooth-bundle constructions inherit ACω; no stronger choice principle is claimed.

load_bearing.statement: For smooth symmetric T and a smooth observer congruence n on nonempty open U, define μ=Tₐᵦnᵃnᵇ, Jᵃ=−Tᵃᵇn_b, Φᵃ=hᵃ_bJᵇ=Jᵃ−μnᵃ, and Sᵃᵇ=hᵃ_chᵇ_dTᶜᵈ.

For smooth symmetric T with ∇ᵃTₐᵦ=0 and observer congruence n on U, ∇ₐJᵃ=−Tᵃᵇ∇ₐn_b and Dμ+μθ+∇ₐΦᵃ=−Tᵃᵇ∇ₐn_b. On an oriented U, a finite smooth singular four-chain with ∂C=Σ₂−Σ₁+B satisfies Φ_J(Σ₂)−Φ_J(Σ₁)=−Φ_J(B)+∫_C(−Tᵃᵇ∇ₐn_b)vol_g.

For an everywhere timelike future-directed Killing field ξ on U, X=√(−g(ξ,ξ)), n=ξ/X, and smooth symmetric divergence-free T, DX=0, aₐ=∇ₐln X, θ=0, ∇ₐJᵃ=−Φᵃaₐ, and ∇ₐ(XJᵃ)=∇ₐ(Tᵃᵇξ_b)=0. Its oriented finite-chain flux balance retains the side flux.

The smooth observer split satisfies nₐΦᵃ=0, Sᵃᵇn_b=0, μ=−Jᵃnₐ and Tᵃᵇ=μnᵃnᵇ+nᵃΦᵇ+nᵇΦᵃ+Sᵃᵇ. This decomposition is unique among the stated smooth scalar, spatial vector and symmetric spatial tensor fields.

In the stated smooth oriented model adopting one field-law presentation, ∇ᵃTₐᵦ=0 and the observer-current local and finite-chain balances hold. With everywhere timelike future Killing ξ and n=ξ/X, Qξ(Σ₂)−Qξ(Σ₁)=−Qξ(B), so equality of charges additionally requires Qξ(B)=0.

concerns.concern: The global-energy bullet says rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions 'already excludes arbitrary rough or noncompact domains from its smooth branch.' The cited scope note excludes distributional sources, boundaries, low regularity and quantum matter; it does not exclude noncompact smooth domains. The actual flux limitation is finite smooth singular chains, and the local identities remain valid on noncompact U. This attribution conflates noncompact ambient domains with integration over unbounded slices.

The 'Smooth and finite branch' bullet places 'noncompact or rough regions' outside the branch 'in the sense of' rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions. That supplier does not impose compactness on the smooth matter domain. The definitions and local lemmas allow arbitrary nonempty open U, and the flat examples use U=R⁴. Clarify that unbounded integration and asymptotic limits are deferred, rather than excluding noncompact smooth domains.

Proof 1.1 refers to 'the prescribed-tensor action sectors.' Under the current post-gr-classical-gravitational-action clause (iii), prescribed dust and perfect-fluid sectors use the direct-equation presentation and do not adopt the variational postulate. The conservation argument is sound through the direct presentation, but this phrase retains an obsolete branch classification.

Example clause 4 describes a 'nonvanishing acceleration source,' and Verification 3.1 concludes that 'its source does not vanish.' The computed source is ρx⁰x¹/X³ and is zero at every point of U with x⁰=0. It is not identically zero on U, which suffices to show that J is not divergence-free on U; the wording should preserve that distinction.

alerts.finding: Statement (d) asserts, for two static observers 'compared over the same coordinate interval Δx⁰,' that Δτ₁/Δτ₂=√(f(r₁)/f(r₂)), without requiring Δx⁰≠0. At Δx⁰=0, clause (c) gives Δτ₁=Δτ₂=0, so the displayed quotient is undefined. Proof 3.1 divides the two increments without checking this denominator. The owner should adjudicate the missing nondegenerate-interval hypothesis or a derivative-based clock-rate formulation.

seams_checked.note: The divergence, Killing-current and finite-chain suppliers are used with their symmetry, smoothness, orientation and side-flux hypotheses intact. However, both owned scope remarks falsely attribute exclusion of noncompact domains to the supplier scope note, and theorem Proof 1.1 calls the prescribed-tensor branches action sectors.
Signature, time orientation, smooth symmetric tensor slot, unit conventions and optional positivity assumptions are preserved. SI flux and momentum restore the distinct factors c and 1/c.
Observer and congruence definitions, spatial projection and rest-space decomposition are preserved; no global tetrad, adapted chart or integrable rest-space distribution is inferred.

Metric compatibility and tensor differentiation support the local calculations. The observer-curve acceleration identity uses the flow parameter, and the physical clock reading remains an adopted assumption. Normal coordinates are invoked only for their first-order scope.
The contracted Bianchi conclusion is divergence-freedom of the Einstein tensor, not covariant constancy. No local gravitational-energy no-go theorem is inferred from normal coordinates.

Dust positivity is retained, perfect-fluid conservation uses both projection equations in the supplier, and the example recovers only the energy projection. Nonzero flat dust is explicitly a prescribed source rather than a field-law solution.
Flat signature, time orientation, smooth tensor construction and units agree with the suppliers; ρ is rest energy density and ρ/c² is rest-mass density.
The flat metric's Christoffel coefficients vanish by the metric-selected connection formula, so the coordinate derivative and divergence computations are legitimate.
Static and boosted fields satisfy the exact future-unit normalization; the boost field is restricted to the timelike wedge. Tensor contractions and spatial projections retain the supplier signs.

The static-congruence lemma uses a=∇ₙn and its spatiality faithfully; its Schwarzschild computation yields a=s/(2r²)∂r. The separately routed zero-interval defect concerns its own clock-rate quotient, not its use of the energy-page supplier.

This is a declared page prerequisite without a substantive citation of the assigned energy results in the inspected page and item uses. The wave page explicitly defers source radiation and energy flux/loss, so it does not promote the finite-chain matter balance into a gravitational-wave energy theorem.
